data.user_prompt: What is Retrieval Probability in AI search?

sections.text:
**Retrieval Probability** is the estimated likelihood that a specific content section gets selected by an AI system during its search phase when generating answers[1]. It represents the foundational layer of Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO), determining whether your content enters the candidate pool that systems like Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, and ChatGPT draw from[1].

If a section is not retrieved, it cannot be cited regardless of its quality or ranking position[1]. This means ranking #1 on Google does not guarantee retrieval, since AI systems select individual sections rather than full pages[1].

## Five Variables That Control Retrieval Probability

Retrieval Probability is influenced by five key factors[1]:

- **Semantic alignment** — how closely a section matches the semantic representation of the query
- **Entity match strength** — the prominence and consistency of entities in the content
- **Structural clarity** — the organization and coherence of the content
- **Topical isolation** — maintaining a single-subject focus
- **Contextual reinforcement** — support from related content clusters

These weights are internal to each AI system and differ across platforms, so Retrieval Probability cannot be computed as a precise formula[1]. Instead, it functions as a diagnostic framework to identify which variable is most likely limiting retrieval for any given content block[1].

## Why It Matters

Retrieval Probability operates as **Layer 1 of the GEO Stack**[1]. Once content is retrieved, it moves to Layer 2 (Extractability), which determines whether it can actually be used in the generated answer[1]. Without successful retrieval at Layer 1, higher optimization layers become irrelevant[1].
